description.narrative:
Building on the project Tax for SDGs and Tax Inspectors without Borders (TIWB), UNDP’s Public finance for SDGs Initiative responds with an strategy built on four strategic pillars: Domestic Resource Mobilization (expanding TIWB programs and implementing systemic tax reforms); Public Expenditure Efficiency (linking revenues to equitable, SDG-aligned spending); Fiscal Policy Coherence (bridging tax, budgeting, debt, and expenditure systemss); and Digital & Data-Driven Public Finance. UNDP’s EQUANOMICS initiative is included as the mechanism to advance gender equality within the PF4SDG.
Impact: Public finance systems at the heart of sustainable development, enabling governments to raise and spend resources more equitably, efficiently, and transparently in support of SDG achievement. Planned Outcomes: The project supports the UNDP 2026-2029 Strategy and the outputs contribute to the outcomes of the 2026-2029 strategic plan: Outcome 1: Prosperity for All Outcome 2: Effective Governance Outcome 3: Crisis Resilience Outcome 4: Healthy Planet. Outputs: Output 1: Strengthened Domestic Resource Mobilization (DRM) for SDG Financing Output 2: Improved Public Expenditure Efficiency & Effectiveness Output 3: Ensuring Fiscal Policy Coherence for Sustainable Development Output 4: Advancing Digitalization & Data-Driven Solutions for Smarter Public Finance
Target group(s) Global constituencies working towards Public Financing for SDG Achievement (including IMF, WB, OECD, UNDESA) Regional constituencies working towards Public Financing for SDG Achievement (including CABRI, ATAF, AFROSAI, ASEAN, PIFS, CIAT, OLACEFS, ECLAC) Country constituencies working towards Public Financing for SDG Achievement (including MOF, MOP, NRA, CB, Audit Institutions, Parliamentary Commissions) Local Governments & Municipal Associations (including UCLG, Local Governments, Local2030 Coalition) Oversight, Transparency & Governance Stakeholders (including INTOSAI, AFROSAI-E, IPU)
